messages:
maria: quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression after the kernel-selector tweak on the H100 pools. 95th token/sec for long seqs dropped ~18% post-rollout. digging in now.

kai: ugh, thanks for flagging. can you paste the profiler/trace? is this across all model sizes or specific to 8k+ sequences?

maria: initial look: mostly for requests >4096. 2 small captures attached below (copied snippets). seems kernel v2 picks a different matmul path that increases mem copies when KV cache hits are frequent.

maria: ```
# perf summary (sample)
model: open-llama-13b
gpu: h100-80gb
seq: 8192
baseline(k1): tokens/s  = 1200
after(k2):      tokens/s  = 985
95th latency baseline = 210ms
95th latency after    = 255ms
kv-cache hit rate ~0.68
KV fragmentation spikes when pkts > 4
```

jess: interesting — KV fragmentation + extra memcpy would wreck throughput. did kernel v2 change the KV layout or just kernel choice?

maria: kernel v2 changes packing -> uses interleaved lanes for matmul to leverage tensor cores, but that forces an extra reorder when we have fragmented KV pages. essentially extra O(N) mem ops per token in worst case.

tyler: idea: reduce max_tokens_per_batch for H100 for long sequences so we avoid huge packed batches that force the interleaved kernel path. keep A100/A10/L4 as-is. low-effort knob while we root-cause.

sam: +1. we should also try kernel v2 with an alternate kernel-config that preserves original KV layout (if possible). can we run a quick AB on a small slice? e2e experiment id: exp-2026-04-h100-kv-ab1

maria: ran an AB yesterday with 2k requests (seq dist skewed to >6k). results: v2 default regressed 17% tokens/s, v2-layoutfix candidate recovered ~95% of baseline but increased small-batch latency a bit. attaching sample flame stacks:

maria: ```
# flame (condensed)
layer  matmul_kernel_v2  42%
layer  kv_reorder        18%
layer  alloc/copy        12%
layer  other             28%
# vs baseline
matmul_kernel_v1  31%
kv_read           6%
alloc/copy        8%
other             55%
```

infra-bot: deploy/exp-2026-04-h100-kv-ab1 started by maria at 2026-04-12T15:03:20Z :rocket:

jess: good signal. two orthogonal short-term actions: 1) lower max_tokens_per_batch for H100 (and maybe A100) for now, 2) add a queue policy tweak to prioritize short tail requests so the big long-seq batches don't sit and accumulate.

tyler: for queue policy: we can implement a soft cap that triggers eager flush if a short request arrives and the head batch currently > X tokens. this reduces head-of-line penalty. propose X=2048 to start.

sam: sounds reasonable. propose a short playbook:
- rollout H100 max_tokens_per_batch: 65536 -> 49152 (reduce by 25%)
- set eager-flush threshold X=2048 for mixed queues only
- run exp on 4 h100 nodes for 4h, measure 95/99 lat and tokens/s, KV fragmentation metric
- if recovered, iterate on kernel-selector config to avoid reorder step

maria: I'm going to create a quick patch for the runtime to expose per-card \"max_tokens_per_batch\" override and queue eager-flush flag. will link PR. planning to roll as a canary to 10% h100 traffic.

kai: please include per-route metrics in the test (long-context chat vs short completions). also track our cost delta since lowering batch token cap could raise unit cost.

maria: yep — will capture token/unit cost + throughput. initial run shows cost +3% but p95 p99 are back within 3% of baseline. need longer run.

jess: if canary looks good, then we keep config while research implements a kernel v2 patch that avoids reorder, or implement a KV defragmentation pass in the runtime. either way we prefer configuration-first mitigations.

sam: i'll spin up perf team to try to reproduce locally with synthetic KV fragmentation. also want kernel vendor to weigh in — filing ticket with vendor perf team.

maria: thanks all. I'll drop the PR and the experiment dashboard link once canary is live. tl;dr: don't push the kernel v2 full rollout for H100 until we evaluate layout-fix candidate; short-term fix: per-card max_tokens_per_batch down 25% + eager-flush for mixed queues. :white_check_mark:
